solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Southerner's horse securing a start in hunt

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece wraps round the others

blocks.note: slang for heroin, like horse
taken as written
in hunting, law is the head start given to the quarry

explanation.surface: A rider from the American South mounts a horse that has got a good start in the hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: Law is an old hunting term for the start allowed to a hunted animal before the hounds are loosed; horse is drug slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: In US history a scalawag was a white Southerner who backed Reconstruction, a sense the word still carries in American usage.

clue.text: Some in school went halves on leaving

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so a piece goes out of the word

blocks.note: going halves on something is sharing it
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Some pupils split the cost before going home.
explanation.walkthrough: SHARED loses RE. 'School' is a school of fish, not a classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Shad are herring-like fish that swim in schools, so they are some members of a school.

clue.text: Red wine catalogue taken by a Midlands soccer team

blocks.note: cat is short for catalogue
taken as written
West Bromwich Albion, a Midlands football club

explanation.surface: A wine list is bought by a football club from the Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: WBA is West Bromwich Albion, an English football club from the West Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Catawba is an American grape variety and the reddish wine made from it.

clue.text: Nearly all changed? Only for fiscals

indicators.note: changed means altered, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Are almost all things altered? Only where tax officials are concerned.
explanation.walkthrough: A procurator fiscal is a Scottish prosecutor, and allenarly is a Scots legal word, so 'for fiscals' marks its register.
explanation.definitionFit: Allenarly is an old Scots term, still found in legal documents, meaning solely or only.

clue.text: The French come with volumes, no end of reading

indicators.note: with no end of a word, its final letter is taken away from the material

blocks.note: gallons are measures of volume
its closing letter

explanation.surface: French readers arrive with books, endlessly reading.
explanation.walkthrough: GALLONS loses the G that ends 'reading'. 'Volumes' suggests books but means measures.
explanation.definitionFit: Allons is French for 'let us go', the call to come along, as in Allons enfants.

clue.text: Thorny stuff catching pedestrian jogging in a wet Beijing

indicators.note: jogging means shaking up, so these letters are jolted into new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Prickly bushes snag a walker out running in rainy Beijing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catching pedestrian' links the definition to the wordplay: the wait-a-bit bush catches walkers on its hooked thorns.
explanation.definitionFit: Wag-n-bietjie, Afrikaans for wait-a-bit, is a South African thorn bush whose hooked spines snag passers-by.

clue.text: Fish unknown in US port

blocks.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A mystery fish turns up in an American harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Gary is an industrial port city in Indiana on the shore of Lake Michigan.

clue.text: Marine creature going round in shallow pool endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is dropped
going round suggests turning about, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a plash is a puddle or shallow pool

explanation.surface: A sea creature circles in a rock pool that seems to go on for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: PLASH loses its H, then PLAS turns round to give SALP.
explanation.definitionFit: A salp is a free-swimming barrel-shaped tunicate of the open sea, so a marine animal.

clue.text: Old scouts very good in shortened Latin-American dance

indicators.note: shortened means cut down, so the final letter is lopped off
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: salsa is a Latin-American dance
pi is short for pious, very good

explanation.surface: Former Scouts behave very well during a short salsa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very good' is the crossword convention for pious; the dance must be cut before it takes the inserted piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Spial is an obsolete word for a spy or scout, so spials are old scouts.

clue.text: Stories about ending of human rights

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece encloses another
the ending of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: lies are made-up stories
its closing letter

explanation.surface: Accounts of the end of human rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Human rights' reads as one phrase, but 'human' only supplies a letter and 'rights' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid, so liens are rights.

clue.text: Changes going round about order of birds

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the outer piece wraps the inner one

blocks.note: a thing that passes into another changes into it
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Things change, going around the order of birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' is the inner piece, not an indicator; 'going round' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: Passeres is the zoological name for the perching birds, the order Passeriformes or its main division.

clue.text: Two chaps prepared meat in eg Dubai

blocks.note: two short names for men, Hal and Al, side by side

explanation.surface: Two men cook a meal while in the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: HAL + AL. The definition reads as an adjective: meat prepared in the Islamic way, as it would be in Dubai.
explanation.definitionFit: Halal describes meat slaughtered and prepared according to Islamic law, standard in Muslim countries such as the UAE.

clue.text: Rock tackles panic arising from gas shortage

indicators.note: to tackle someone is to grab and hold them, so the outer piece takes hold of the inner one
panic arising suggests something stirred up, so its letters are thrown into new order

blocks.note: aa is rough, clinkery lava, a crossword staple
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rock musician deals with panic attacks brought on by running out of gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Acapnia is a medical term for a deficiency of carbon dioxide in the blood.

clue.text: Concerned with a strong Union, unlimited state ceremony organised

indicators.note: without limits means the outer letters are stripped, leaving the inside
organised means arranged anew, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: its inner letters
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A grand state ceremony arranged to celebrate a strong political union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a political federation, but it is a bond, as made by cement.
explanation.definitionFit: Cementatory means relating to cementing, the process that makes a firm bond or union.

clue.text: Police releasing pirates as before

indicators.note: to police something is to put it in order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Officers letting captured pirates go, just as they did last time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police' reads as a noun but works as a verb meaning put in order. 'As before' marks the sense as old.
explanation.definitionFit: Algerines were the Barbary corsairs sailing from Algiers, so the historical word for those pirates.

clue.text: No honeyed drink brought back or spirit

indicators.note: brought back means returned the way it came, so the letters are read from the end

blocks.note: taken as written
mead is wine made from honey

explanation.surface: A refusal of mead brought out again, or else some other liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: NO + MEAD reversed gives DAEMON. 'Spirit' looks like alcohol, but it is a supernatural being.
explanation.definitionFit: A daemon is a guardian spirit or demigod in Greek thought.

clue.text: Triplets, primarily accommodated in space done up, stop me moving house

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the initial letter is kept
accommodated in means housed within, so the letter sits inside
in a down entry, up means the letters run backwards towards the top

blocks.note: room means space
its opening letter
ho is an old call to stop, like whoa
taken as written

explanation.surface: Parents of triplets, short of room, beg someone to stop them moving house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving house' reads as relocating, but it means a house that moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorhome is a vehicle fitted out as living quarters, literally a house on the move.

clue.text: Scratching face, old Scotsman with a beard

indicators.note: scratching out the face of a word wipes away its front letter

blocks.note: Sawny, a form of Sandy, was an old nickname for a Scot

explanation.surface: An old Scotsman with a beard scratches his face.
explanation.walkthrough: SAWNY loses its S. The beard is the bristly awn of a grass or cereal head.
explanation.definitionFit: Awny means having awns, the bristles that make barley look bearded.

clue.text: Perk up Dad, and face time of being old

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters run backwards towards the top

blocks.note: pa is a word for father
pan is slang for the face
age is the period of being old

explanation.surface: Cheer up your father and confront the onset of old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perk up' looks like one phrase meaning cheer; 'Perk' is the definition and 'up' the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An appanage is a perquisite, originally land granted to a younger royal child for support.

clue.text: Emerge from fence, villain finally nicked

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it, the only one kept
nicked means taken away, so a letter is stolen out of the word

blocks.note: to fence a field is to enclose it
its closing letter

explanation.surface: A villain escapes from a fence before finally being caught.
explanation.walkthrough: ENCLOSE loses an N. 'Fence' and 'nicked' suggest a receiver of stolen goods and an arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclose is the biologist's verb for an insect emerging from its pupa or egg.

clue.text: Evil is found in trade by exchange — sign of a bastard

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: barter is trading goods without money
a sin is an evil act
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wickedness turns up in bartering, the mark of a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Evil' and 'is' go inside together. 'Bastard' is no insult here: it means a child born outside marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The bar sinister is the popular name for the heraldic mark said to denote illegitimate descent.

clue.text: Always storing cut of meat in old conveyor

indicators.note: storing means keeping inside, so the outer piece holds the inner

blocks.note: e'er is the poetic short form of ever
loin is a cut of meat

explanation.surface: An old conveyor belt that always carries cuts of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conveyor' suggests a belt; here it is a person who conveys things away.
explanation.definitionFit: An eloiner, an archaic legal word, is one who removes or carries goods away out of reach.

clue.text: Molar apt to play up? Ingest one

definitions.text: Molar apt to play up? Ingest one
definitions.note: the whole clue: what to swallow for a troublesome tooth

indicators.note: something playing up misbehaves, so these letters will not stay in order
to ingest is to take inside, so the shuffled letters swallow another piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A tooth liable to ache, so take a painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read as wordplay it builds the answer, and read plainly it prescribes the tablet for toothache.
explanation.definitionFit: Paracetamol is the common painkilling pill a person with an aching tooth would swallow.

clue.text: One born Elizabeth to become senior sister

blocks.note: a means one
b is the abbreviation for born
Bess is a pet form of Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A girl christened Elizabeth goes on to become head of a convent.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbess is the head of an abbey of nuns, a senior religious sister.

clue.text: Fruit and nuts unopened

indicators.note: not opened means the opening letter is missing

blocks.note: bananas is slang for crazy, as is nuts

explanation.surface: A sealed bag of fruit and nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: BANANAS loses its B. 'Fruit and nuts' reads as a snack, but 'nuts' means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Ananas is another name for the pineapple, a tropical fruit.

clue.text: Neighbour swallows Liberal line pretty much

indicators.note: something that swallows takes other things inside itself

blocks.note: to abut is to border on, as a neighbour does
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A nearby politician pretty much accepts the Liberal party line.
explanation.walkthrough: A(L L)BUT. 'Neighbour' must be read as a verb, to lie next to.
explanation.definitionFit: All but is an idiom meaning almost or very nearly, the same as pretty much.

clue.text: Looks good for mathematician's term

blocks.note: lo is an old word for look, twice
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A mathematician's word for good looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looks' is a plural verb: two lo's, each meaning look!
explanation.definitionFit: Lolog is a mathematician's term for the logarithm of a logarithm.

clue.text: Favourite place for relatives

blocks.note: first meaning: a bro is a place one is fond of, a Chambers sense, here plural
second meaning: short for brothers

explanation.walkthrough: The plural of the first sense works only loosely with the singular 'place'; the second is the familiar short form.
explanation.definitionFit: Bros is informal for brothers, who are close relatives, and Chambers also gives bro as a cherished place.

clue.text: Small fly found in cored apples perhaps

indicators.note: coring removes the centre, so the middle letter comes out

blocks.note: apples are an example of fruit

explanation.surface: A tiny fly turns up inside cored apples.
explanation.walkthrough: FRUIT loses its middle U. 'Perhaps' shows that apples are only an example of the word wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The frit fly is a small fly whose larvae damage cereal crops.

clue.text: An event touring Alaska shows rare horses

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: 'this' can stand for an event being referred to, as in 'this is what happened'
AK is the US postal code for Alaska

explanation.surface: A travelling show in Alaska features rare breeds of horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The link from 'an event' to its block is loose: the pronoun points at whatever is happening, as in 'this is it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Takhi is the Mongolian name for Przewalski's horse, a rare wild horse species.

clue.text: Second year students issuing positive notes

indicators.note: issuing means going out, so a letter leaves the word

blocks.note: sophs is short for sophomores, US second-year students
P is the abbreviation for positive

explanation.surface: Second-year students hand out encouraging notes.
explanation.walkthrough: SOPHS loses P. 'Notes' are musical notes, not written messages.
explanation.definitionFit: Soh is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale, so sohs are musical notes.

clue.text: Champ rallies on getting eagles

indicators.note: to champ is to chew noisily, and chewed things are mangled out of shape

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports champion recovers and goes on to win the Eagles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champ' looks like a champion but is the verb to chew.
explanation.definitionFit: An allerion is a heraldic eagle shown without beak or feet.

clue.text: Work with willow is comparatively dense

blocks.note: a machine that works is said to go
an osier is a willow used in basketry

explanation.surface: Working with willow wood is a fairly heavy job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dense' means stupid here, not compact: a goose is a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: Goosy means foolish like a goose, so goosier is more foolish, more dense.

clue.text: Skirt length one backed for dancing girl

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so the joined pieces are read from the end

blocks.note: the hem is the edge or skirt of a garment
L is the abbreviation for length
a means one

explanation.surface: A skirt of some length, supported by someone, for a dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: An almeh is an Egyptian professional dancing and singing girl.

clue.text: Troops used after ending of police protection

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept
used after puts one piece behind the other in the answer

blocks.note: its closing letter
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers are deployed once the police can no longer guard people.
explanation.definitionFit: Egis is a variant spelling of aegis, meaning protection or sponsorship.

clue.text: They arrange meets and after removing wheel, sort tyres out

indicators.note: removing means a letter is taken away from the material
sorted out means put into a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: O is round, like a wheel
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Mechanics who organise race meetings sort out tyres once the wheel comes off.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the O out of SORT TYRES, then rearrange. 'Meets' are secret meetings, not sporting fixtures.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryster is one who arranges a tryst, an appointment to meet, typically between lovers.
